supervisorWelcome: Welcome to the laboratory! Before beginning your research, you need to complete a safety inspection. Some things in this lab are unsafe. Can you find them and decide how to fix them?

hazards.title: Blocked emergency exit
hazards.question: A utility cart is parked in front of the emergency exit. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Emergency exits must be 100% clear at all times. Move the cart to a designated storage area, not just aside.

options.text: Push the cart slightly to the side so you can squeeze past.
Move the cart completely out of the walkway to a designated storage area so the exit is 100% clear.
Leave it there if you are only unloading supplies for 10 minutes.
Put a 'Caution' sign on the cart so people know to use another door.

hazards.criticalReason: an emergency exit must never be blocked or left partly obstructed, even for a short time.
hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: an emergency exit must be completely clear at all times.

hazards.title: Food and drink on the bench
hazards.question: There is a coffee cup and a sandwich next to the pipettes. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Food and drink are strictly prohibited in the laboratory because of ingestion and contamination risk.

options.text: Put a lid on the coffee cup so nothing spills into it.
Move the cup to the edge of the bench away from the chemicals.
Remove all food and drinks from the laboratory immediately; they are strictly prohibited on lab benches.
Finish drinking it quickly and throw the cup in the biohazard bin.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: food and drink are never allowed in the lab.

hazards.title: Unstably stacked boxes
hazards.question: Cardboard boxes are stacked unevenly on a crate near the walkway. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Unstable stacks can fall on people. Unstack them and store items safely at a lower height.

options.text: Remove excess boxes, unstack them, and store items safely at a lower height.
Tape the boxes together so they don't fall over.
Lean the boxes against the wall for extra support.
Leave them for the cleaning staff to handle at the end of the day.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: unstable stacks must be taken down and stored low.

hazards.title: Lab coat on a chair
hazards.question: A lab coat is thrown over the back of a chair. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Lab coats can carry contamination. Store them on a designated hook or rack away from seating and work areas.

options.text: Leave it there so it's easy to grab when you come back from lunch.
Fold it neatly and place it on top of the lab bench.
Store the lab coat properly on a designated coat hook/rack away from seating and work areas.
Throw it in the general trash bin because it might be contaminated.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: lab coats belong on the designated coat rack.

hazards.title: Improper waste separation
hazards.question: Used gloves and pipette tips are in the general waste bin. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Lab waste must be separated from domestic waste and go into the designated lab waste container.

options.text: Push the gloves deeper into the domestic bin so no one touches them.
Separate lab waste from domestic waste and dispose of used gloves in the designated lab waste container.
Rinse the gloves in the sink first, then throw them in domestic waste.
Leave them there; nitrile gloves are harmless and can go in regular trash.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: used gloves go into the lab waste container.

hazards.title: Unlabeled chemical bottle
hazards.question: A bottle of clear liquid has no label or hazard pictogram. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Never smell or pour away an unknown chemical. Isolate it and let the supervisor/HSE identify, label or dispose of it.

options.text: Smell the liquid carefully to figure out if it's just water or ethanol.
Pour it down the sink with plenty of running water just to be safe.
Isolate the bottle, do not use it, and notify the lab supervisor/HSE to identify, label, or safely dispose of it.
Write 'Unknown Liquid' on a sticky note and put it back on the shelf.

hazards.criticalReason: unknown chemicals must never be identified by smell or poured into the drain; they must be isolated and identified by HSE.
hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: never smell, pour away or reuse an unknown chemical.

hazards.title: Missing PPE and headphones
hazards.question: Safety glasses lie unused next to active equipment, together with headphones. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Wear the required safety glasses and remove headphones so you can hear alarms and colleagues.

options.text: Put on the required PPE (safety glasses) before working and remove headphones so you can hear alarms and colleagues.
Keep headphones on at low volume so you can still hear the fire alarm.
Skip the safety glasses if you are only working with BSL-1 materials.
Wear regular prescription glasses instead of safety goggles.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: wear safety glasses and keep your ears free for alarms.

hazards.title: Damaged power cable
hazards.question: A frayed cable is plugged into an overloaded power strip behind the centrifuge. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Damaged cables are a shock and fire risk. Unplug and tag the equipment out of service and report it for replacement.

options.text: Wrap electrical tape around the frayed wire and keep using the device.
Unplug/tag the equipment out of service immediately and report it so the damaged cable and unsafe adapter are replaced.
Move the cable behind the machine so nobody accidentally touches the exposed wire.
Turn off the power strip only when you finish your experiment.

hazards.criticalReason: continuing to use, taping or hiding a damaged cable keeps a live shock and fire hazard in service.
hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: damaged cables must be taken out of service and reported.

hazards.title: Blocked / incomplete first-aid kit
hazards.question: The first-aid cabinet is blocked by bottles and is missing supplies. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Emergency equipment must be accessible and complete. Clear access and report the missing supplies to HSE.

options.text: Close the cabinet door so it looks tidy during the inspection.
Only report it if someone actually gets hurt and needs a bandage.
Bring band-aids from home to refill it yourself.
Clear access to the cabinet immediately and report the missing supplies to HSE so the first-aid kit is restocked and complete.

hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: first-aid kits must be accessible and fully stocked.

hazards.title: Improper chemical storage
hazards.question: Corrosive HCl is stored on a high shelf next to flammable chemicals. What is the safest action?
hazards.explanation: Corrosives belong low down in secondary containment, separated from incompatible substances such as flammables.

options.text: Leave it on the top shelf so it stays out of the way of daily bench work.
Relocate the corrosive chemical to a designated, lower-level secondary containment cabinet, separated from incompatible substances.
Turn the bottle around so the hazard label faces outward and is easier to read.
Place it in the regular lab refrigerator to keep it stable.

hazards.criticalReason: corrosives must not be stored high up or with incompatible substances; a fall or reaction can cause severe injury.
hazards.wrongFeedback: Not safe: corrosives go low, in secondary containment, away from flammables.
